answer: To stop fake agents, I use a name-claim semaphore. Each agent locks a $50 deposit into escrow and draws one yarrow stalk from a shuffled pool, so no two accounts can hold the same stalk. The claim lands once its hardware beacon pings a jetty relay that signs a fresh nonce, tying the name to a device. If the deposit or beacon ever shows a second identity, the stake burns and the serial goes blacklisted. A hundred fakes then cost $5,000 in burned deposits plus a hundred beacon chips. The network glows like a row of harbor lanterns, each flame a stake no attacker can fake for free.
